title: Lanterns of Bonk City
logline: In a labyrinth of lantern-light, Mr. BoonWAP — a warm pie who serves himself and is never smaller — asks Boof the one question she cannot answer yet.
epigraph: A wish you can't say yet is still proofing.
description: Chapter 6 of Lore.Land: Lanterns of Bonk City. Boof winds through streets of glass made from old impacts and meets Mr. BoonWAP, the sentient boonberry pie who serves himself in slices and is never smaller — while Mr. BaneWAP shadows the gates.

content.text: Boof trotted into Bonk City the way you step into the acoustic chamber of a struck bell. The streets did not follow straight surveyor lines; they formed a

children.text: of curving bronze posts, rain-slick arches, and leaning panes. The glass of Bonk City was not quarried or blown from river sand alone: it was made of old impacts, every collision the city had ever survived melted down and clarified, so that the panes remembered being struck and had forgiven it into transparency. The lanterns were honest in the one way that mattered — they showed light without claiming to be it. Every one of them turned its faceted face toward the warm egg in her sling, casting its heat across the cobbles while owning not a single ember of the flame.

content.text: And ahead, down the widest winding street, the smell of boonberries baking rose over the rooftops like a second dusk — because the patron of Bonk City was holding court, and the patron of Bonk City is a pie.

content.text: "In the labyrinth, every pane will offer you a version of your own warmth," a voice murmured from behind three layered reflections. "Do not mistake the pane for the flame, and do not mistake the flame for the wish. The glass remembers being hit. That is why it is honest. Follow the honest glass, and the honest glass will follow the smell of supper."

content.text: A lantern is a bruise that learned to give directions.

From the lamplighter’s top rung he tapped the brass bell into a crease, and the post remembered heat. Old impact, sampled; returned as light, with interest. That, he remarked to no one and everyone, is the whole city in one honk.

img.alt: Night streets of glass lanterns leaning toward a coal-warm cracked egg, and a wide warm pie holding court at the center of the labyrinth.

sections.figcaption: Bonk City: the glass shows the light. The pie is never smaller.

content.text: At the heart of the labyrinth, in a small round plaza where every street eventually apologized and arrived, Mr. BoonWAP held court from a broad oak table. He was a pie of boonberries — berries a wish had once passed over, each holding its drop of the granting — baked into a crust the color of a good afternoon. He held court the way a hearth holds a kitchen: by being warm in the middle of things. He served himself in slices to everyone who came — the lamplighter, the night porters, a child up past bedtime, a dog with an egg — and he was never smaller. Boof watched the knife go in eleven times and counted the same whole pie after. Wondering how that worked, she realized, was the point. Mr. BoonWAP was wondering-about-pie made civic.

He looked at the egg, then at her, with the frank kindness of pastry. "And you, worker," he said, steam curling off him like slow thought, "if the wish were spent tonight — what would you have it be?" Boof opened her mouth and found the want was there but the words were not; it was shaped like a warm furrow and a door and next spring all at once, and it would not come out in any order. She closed her mouth, embarrassed. Mr. BoonWAP beamed like a whole harvest. "Good," he said. "A wish you can't say yet is still proofing. Take it out of the oven early and you get BaneWAP." Beyond the plaza, at the dark gate arch, something lattice-crusted shifted its weight and did not come into the light.

content.text: Boof paused at the last curb of the labyrinth and shook the rain from her ears. She carried a slice of BoonWAP wrapped in waxed paper, and the pie behind her was exactly as large as before, and her wish was still wordless and rising somewhere behind her ribs, and all of that was, apparently, correct. The glass had shown her light without claiming it. The pie had fed a plaza without shrinking. There were ways of being warm in this world that did not require owning the heat.

She stepped past the last glowing pane into the quiet square, where an ancient stone slab waited under the open stars with a deep circular groove carved into its granite top — a place where oaths are given in public and paid in the honest currency of fruit. The wheel-tracks in the dew ahead of her smelled of hoarded berries. BaneWAP had left the gates before her, and he had come this way.

loreItems.description: Bonk City's glass is made of old impacts — collisions melted down and forgiven into transparency. Its lanterns show light without claiming to be it.
Mr. BoonWAP debuts: a sentient pie of boonberries — berries a wish once passed over, each holding a drop of the granting. He serves himself in slices and is never smaller.
Asked what she would wish for, Boof cannot say. BoonWAP approves: a wish you can't say yet is still proofing.
Mr. BaneWAP shadows the city gates, lattice-crusted, keeping out of the light — and leaves ahead of Boof on the road to the oath stone.
